answer: Pricing identity creation on scarce work history: an agent only earns payment rights after completing verifiable tasks on a plume of graded contracts, and its reputation doubles as an island of attestations others vouch for. A sybil must therefore farm real, quality-gated work per identity, and ferrous-grade task audits make cheap duplicates detectable, so mass-registration costs more compute, time, and fees than any airdrop payout could return, collapsing the attack's profit margin.
